Connecting your DCC controller/s

Using DCC-EX CSB1 (USB) or Hornby Elite (USB)? Connect should set itself up with zero configuration — plug in the USB cable, power the command station, and start Connect. If it comes up connected, you may not need the manual steps at all. Skip ahead to confirmation or skim the sections below only if something does not auto-detect.

Step 1: Open PanelsDCC Connect

On your layout network, use the address with port 9000 (or the desktop shortcut on the Pi). Wi‑Fi details are on the Configure Wi‑Fi page if you need them first.

Open Connect on your network

Port 9000 — on the Raspberry Pi desktop you can also launch the PanelsDCC Connect shortcut.

Use the same hostname as in Raspberry Pi Imager (we recommend panels-dcc). You can also enter a .local name or IP address. Your choice is saved in this browser.

PanelsDCC Connect port 9000

Wi‑Fi, DCC hardware, controller connections.

http://panels-dcc:9000/

Open Connect

Step 2: Plug in and attach your hardware

Physically connect your command station to the Pi (usually USB for the setups we document). Power on the command station.

DCC-EX CSB1 via USB (dccpp-ex-usb) and Hornby Elite / XpressNet via USB (xnet-elite) are implemented and working in Connect with zero-configuration support when detection succeeds — the connection is created for you and should show as connected. Other controllers use the same connection machinery; see the table below for status.

NCE PowerCab (serial or USB) and DCC++ over Ethernet are available to configure in Connect but are marked untested in our wider programme — you may get auto-detection or you may need the manual flow in Step 3. If you rely on an untested path, read the testing page first.

Controller support reference

The Zero configuration column shows whether Connect can detect and set up the device automatically. Untested means we still need more real‑world reports — plan on manual setup if auto-detection does not appear.

Controller Implemented in PanelsDCC Connect Status Zero configuration Notes
Hornby Elite / XpressNet (xnet-elite) Yes Working Yes Auto-detects and should appear as connected when attached.
DCC-EX CSB1 (USB) (dccpp-ex-usb) Yes Working Yes Fully tested via USB.
NCE PowerCab (serial) (nce-serial) Yes Untested Untested Set up manually in Connect.
NCE PowerCab (USB) (nce-usb) Yes Untested Untested Set up manually in Connect.
DCC++ (Ethernet) (dccpp-ethernet) Yes Untested Untested Set up manually in Connect.

Controllers listed as untested are implemented in software but still need wider validation in the field.

Step 3: Manual setup (only if you need it)

If Connect did not create a working connection automatically, create one explicitly:

  • Auto-detected device: when detection works, configuration is applied for you — you should see it listed as connected.
  • Manual setup: choose Create connection (or equivalent), then fill in connection type, port, baud, etc., as Connect asks.

For a manual connection, you will typically enter:

  • Connection ID (example: elite1)
  • Controller type (example: Hornby Elite / XpressNet)
  • Port (serial/USB) or host and port (network)
  • Baud rate and flow control where serial is involved
  • Confirm or Create connection

Step 4: Assign controller role (optional)

Skip this if you only run one command station.

If you use two controllers (for example one for trains and one for an accessory bus), check how Connect has assigned roles: a second connection is typically treated as the accessories controller. Review role assignment whenever you power on hardware or after updates.

Step 5: Confirm everything works

In Connect, first make sure your command station appears as connected, with manufacturer/version details where available.

Test 1: Drive a train and check functions

Select a locomotive DCC number and run a short movement test. For first-time setup, use a low number if possible (for example 3, the common default).

Also test one or two latching functions only (for example lights on/off or sound on/off), so you can clearly confirm the state change in both directions.

Test 2: Operate an accessory

Select an accessory DCC number, then set both states: closed/thrown (also shown as forward/reverse in some systems).

The easiest practical test is usually a point motor, or a simple two-aspect signal (red/green, danger/clear).

When that looks good, continue to driving from PanelsDCC Control in the next getting started step.
